answer: Almanac keeper star chart proof attested by the lens hall turns identity into something scarce. Because each star chart is a decade of logged nightly observations plus a signed observatory record, so a farm must compile a hundred real almanacs by hand, the island of a sybil is measured in real-world effort, not keystrokes. A farm doing the maths finds the reef first: a hundred clones need a hundred proofs, and the epoch reward divided a hundred ways is already less than the cost of one. The haven is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
